I was under the, in retrospect, naive assumption that the Senate would actually move a product that we could go to conference with, and that the White House would want to get comprehensive housing finance reform done. In dealing with Secretary Geithner at the time, I was convinced he wanted to get this done. And then unfortunately when the Senate moved their bill roughly a year after we moved our bill, we were into the campaign season and it was clear to me that the Obama White House was not interested in an election year. For whatever reason, after Secretary Geithner left, and Secretary Lew came in. My sense was Secretary Lew had no interest in the topic, which, in the president, had no interest in the topic. And so this is heavy political lifting. And there are very few people who want to take it on unless they see a path to getting a bill on the president's desk. Unless the president signals that he won't sit on his desk, most people don't want to engage in the heavy lifting and tip-dowing through the political minefield. I know I'm mixing metaphors, but trust hopefully your readers and listeners can figure out what I'm saying. Most don't want to do it. So, I feel the Trump administration wants to get this done. And I understand that. They've taken longer than I would have hoped, but I still think it's a priority. And I think conditions are ripe hopefully in the next Congress to get this done.
